newsitem.title: RUSSIA: Yeltsin leaves Moscow for Helsinki summit.
newsitem.headline: Yeltsin leaves Moscow for Helsinki summit.

text.p: Russian President Boris Yeltsin left for Helsinki on Thursday for a summit meeting with U.S. President Bill Clinton, the Kremlin press service said.
Television footage showed Yeltsin dressed in a long dark coat mounting the steps of his plane at the Vnukovo-2 government airport, accompanied by his wife Naina, in a flurry of snow.

Prime Minister Viktor Chernomyrdin and other officials saw Yeltsin off at the airport. The president, firmly back at the helm after months of illness, strode confidently up the steps of his brand-new presidential plane, an Ilyushin Il-96, which set off for the Finnish capital just after 2 p.m. (1100 GMT).
NATO's plans for eastward expansion are expected to top the summit's agenda, which will also include bilateral economic relations and arms control in Europe.

Russian officials have stepped up their verbal offensive against NATO's plans on the eve of the summit, saying they were the West's biggest mistake since the end of the Cold War. Moscow regards NATO's intention of admitting former communist countries in eastern and central Europe as a threat to its own security.

Yeltsin and Clinton, who arrived in Helsinki earlier on Thursday, were to meet on Thursday evening at a dinner hosted by Finnish President Martti Ahtisaari. The main talks start on Friday morning. Yeltsin returns to Moscow on Saturday.
